Vs.

full_judgment: "11. Mr. Anil Chandra Sarker, learned Advocate for the appellant, has contended that it was for the pre-emptor to lead evidence showing that the left-out co-sharers had lost their interest in the land in question by transfer or otherwise and that the High Court Division illegally shifted the burden of proof upon the pre-emptee in this respect. It is not disputed that the left-out persons are co-sharers by inheritance. But there is no evidence whatever to show that they got no subsisting interest in the land under pre-emption, Mr. Yeasin, the learned Advocate for the respondent, has failed to show us how it could be held that the left-out co-sharers lost or transferred their interest in the land under pre-emption. The onus of proof in this respect is upon the preemptor but his onus has not been discharged. The observation of the High Court Division as quoted above shows that it was for the preemptee to lead evidence to the effect that the 'left-out co-sharers still got interest in the land sought to be pre-empted. The High Court Division in this connection relied upon the decision of Motilal Sikder's case in which it was observed that the positive injunction as to parties under section 96(2) is directory. The facts of this case as set out above are not attracted by the decision in Motilal's case. On the contrary, these facts are attracted by the decision in the case of Abdus Samad vs. Sohrab Ali in which it has been held that non-joinder of parties who got right of pre-emption is fatal to the proceeding."
